title: Site preferrer: latency & network-health scoring policy for region selection
creator: Asha Patel
description:
Background:
The georouter currently uses a simple p50 threshold and a crude retry on failure. As we onboard more dedicated capacity and private deployments with varying network characteristics, we need a robust site selection policy that combines latency percentiles (p50/p95) with network health signals (packet loss, jitter, upstream errors) to choose a primary region and a ranked fallback set.

Goal:
Design and implement a scoring policy (Site Preferrer) that: 1) ranks candidate sites by a composite score built from p50, p95, and network health; 2) supports tier-aware routing (hosted/dedicated/private) with configurable penalties; 3) includes hysteresis and cooldown to avoid flapping; 4) provides deterministic mapping to fallback model variants (quantized vs full-precision) when switching across tiers; 5) is observable, testable, and rollback-safe.

Non-goals:
- This ticket does not change LB infra or client SDK routing logic. It provides the scoring/policy service used by the router.

Proposed scoring model (high level):
- Inputs for each candidate site: p50, p95 (ms), packet_loss (%), jitter (ms), recent 5xx rate (%), capacity_utilization (%). Lookback window: 5m for short-term signals, 1h for trend smoothing.
- Normalize latency: using a capped sigmoid mapping to [0,1] per metric to avoid outliers dominating. Eg norm_p50 = sigmoid((p50 - baseline_p50)/scale). Baselines per region are learned from historical medians.
- Composite score = w1*norm_p50 + w2*norm_p95 + w3*net_penalty where net_penalty = clamp(packet_loss*alpha + jitter_norm*beta + 5xx_rate*gamma). Default weights: w1=0.25, w2=0.5, w3=0.25 (favor tail latency).
- Tier penalty: hosted=0, dedicated= -0.05 (slight boost), private= -0.02, but also allow per-customer overrides. Penalties are additive to score to reflect contractual preferences.
- Hysteresis & stickiness: only switch primary if candidate score is lower by delta>0.08 for at least 3 consecutive evaluation windows, and require a cooldown (default 30s) between switches.
- Fallback variant mapping: each site exposes supported model variants and a priority list (e.g., fp16, int8-quant). When a switch crosses tier boundaries (hosted -> dedicated) or when capacity_utilization > 85%, the router should pick the top supported variant within the target site that satisfies quality constraints. If none meet quality constraints, fallback to next-ranked site.

Observability & SLOs:
- Expose per-decision metrics: chosen_site, score_breakdown (p50_component, p95_component, net_penalty, tier_penalty), reason_code (safety-flip, score-gap, capacity-evict).
- Dashboards: per-customer route heatmap, site score trends, churn rate (switches/min), rollback events.
- Alerts: unexpected churn > 2/min or p95 increase to customers after switch > 20%.

Acceptance criteria:
- Unit tests for scoring math, normalization, and hysteresis logic.
- Integration test: simulated sites with synthetic telemetry produce deterministic selection across scenarios (degraded tail latency, packet loss spike, capacity limits).
- Canary rollout plan defined and automated: start with 1% of traffic on staging then 10% on non-critical customers.
- Dashboard and metrics emitted to prod telemetry.
- Documentation: runtime docs and example config for per-customer overrides.

Implementation plan (phases):
1) Proof-of-concept scoring library (go): standalone package with deterministic inputs and tests. (2 d)
2) Integrate POC into routing service as a feature flagged decision module. Add metrics and logs. (5 d)
3) Add fallback variant mapping & per-customer overrides; expand tests. (3 d)
4) Canary and rollback automation, dashboards. (3 d)

Dependencies and open questions:
- Need consolidated telemetry stream for packet loss/jitter per site (ENG-502815).
- How to obtain per-region baseline medians for normalization (aggregation job exists but needs tuning).
- Policy configuration UIs in Console (PM/Design to scope later).

Risks and mitigations:
- Flapping: addressed via hysteresis + cooldown.
- Overfitting weights: expose weights as runtime-config and validate via A/B tests.
- Quality regressions when switching quantized variants: require correlation checks with evals or restrict automated variant switches to non-critical traffic until validated.

Links to artifacts:
- Design doc (internal): https://confluence.redwood.ai/smart-routing/site-preferrer-design
- Telemetry ticket: sources/linear/engineering/ENG-502815-network-telemetry-consolidation.json
- PR template: https://github.com/redwood-inference/router/pulls
acceptance_criteria: Scoring library implemented with unit tests for normalization and weighting
Routing service can use feature-flagged Site Preferrer and emits score components to metrics
Integration tests covering latency tail spikes, packet loss, and capacity constraints pass deterministically
Canary rollout plan exists and is executable; rollback triggers defined
Console docs and runtime configuration examples published
